title: Made a video analysis of David Cronenberg’s Crash

commenti.body: I would love to watch this essay, but Crash is regarded extremely poorly in my country. It begs the question, how does one go into a famously hated film? Crash, Morbius, Howard the Duck, Catwoman. The fear of watching utter trash sits on the brow of the potential viewer. Do you think Crash is worth watching?

All the other films mentioned are either products of large studios or based off pretty sprawling source material, whereas Crash is a film made by an auteur with a singular vision. Not everyone is going to like it, but I'd watch it for the experience alone, which even those who dislike the film tend to acknowledge is a unique one. The essay spoils the entire movie but you could probably watch it as a substitute, just know you'll only be getting the narrative and not the experience itself.
You’ve intrigued me! It’s considered the least deserving best picture winner in Oscar history! I’m going to give it a go!
Oh no, you've got it confused! There are two movies with the title Crash, this is a completely different one from the best picture winner. 1996, not 2004 haha. No relation to each other.
Dear God people don’t make the mistake I did! 2 hours of the other Crash. That won so many awards? I watched it intently to make sure I fully appreciated your video. Ugh!
Hahahahhaha. This was a funny thread
Is your country perhaps West Imbeciliana?
As soon as I saw your first comment I immediately wondered if you were mistaking it with the 2004 film lmao

Im not as well versed in film (particularly older film) as many others are so perhaps i'm not drawing from a sufficiently large set of films, but to this day Crash remains the most memorable and expressive film I've ever seen; it is utterly unforgettable. 

The cinematography is unbelievably good, probably Peter Suschitzky's best work, which is saying a lot. 

Thematically it's brilliant as well. The dissonance of the violent crashes with sexuality is almost Carrollian in a way.
